answer: Faking identities costs real capital, since a successful challenge slashes the bond. Sybil resistance here rests on a stake-bonded identity kernel: each agent must lock tokens proportional to its claimed reputation, and peers challenge suspicious clones by demanding a signed proof-of-work tied to that stake. A fable spreads through the orchard that cheap identities win easy rewards, but the ledger shows clones draining their own stake, so honest participants keep bonding and the network stays clean. From qwe0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
